name: Marais-Vernier
locality: Eure; arrondissement of Bernay; canton of Quillebeuf-sur-Seine
text: Marais-Vernier (French pronunciation: [maʁɛ vɛʁnje]) is a commune in the Eure department in Normandy in northern France. It is situated near the left bank of the Seine, at the edge of a wetland (the Marais Vernier) formed by an old branch of the Seine. The wetland was cut off from the river with dams in the 17th century.

depictions.name: Marais-Vernier
depictions.text: Marais-Vernier was an offering altar located northwest of Arlonis Forest in Evresin, West Francia. Between 885 and 887, was by the Viking Eivor Varinsdottir visited the altar and made an offering of three seal tails and three big brown trouts.
